title: Dimension inequality for finite type algebras over a Noetherian domain
statement:
Let $R\subset S$ be an inclusion of commutative domains, with $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For primes $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ with $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$, write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(R/\mathfrak p)$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{Frac}(S/\mathfrak q)$, and let $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r)$ be the supremum of lengths of strict chains of primes ending at $\mathfrak r$. With transcendence degree as in [def-kun-transcendence-degree] ($\operatorname{trdeg}_RS$ being that of the $R$-algebra $S$), one has
$$
\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\leq \operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{R}S-\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q).
$$

proof.text: First handle an algebra $S=R[x]$ generated by one element. The evaluation map $f:P=R[T]\twoheadrightarrow S$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak n$, since $S$ is a domain, and $\mathfrak n\cap R=0$ by the inclusion $R\subset S$. If $\mathfrak n=0$, evaluation is an $R$-algebra isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-prime-height-residue-degree] to the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$: it gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_R S=1$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+t=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+1$, where $t=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. This is the desired additive inequality, with equality.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case I and the one-generator kernel dichotomy

proof.text: If $\mathfrak n\ne0$, apply [lem-trf-monogenic-quotient-height-drop] to $f$. It gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_R S=0$, identifies the residue fields over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and gives $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+1\leq\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ for $Q=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The polynomial formula gives $\operatorname{ht}(Q)+t=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+1$. Add $t$ to the inequality and cancel $1$, obtaining $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+t\leq\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)$. Thus the same bound holds for every one-generator domain inclusion.

source.place: Tag 02IJ (algebra-lemma-dimension-formula), Case II, using the Case I formula

proof.text: Induct on the length $n$ of a finite algebra-generating list. With $n=0$ the inclusion is $R=S$; heights agree and both degrees are zero. For $n>0$ put $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]\subset S$ and $\mathfrak r=\mathfrak q\cap A$. The ring $A$ is a domain as a subring, and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Apply induction to $R\subset A$ and Steps 1–2 to $A\subset S=A[x_n]$. Write the resulting additive inequalities as $h_r+u\leq h_p+a$ and $h_q+v\leq h_r+b$. The field-tower statement gives $u+v=t$, and the domain-tower statement gives $a+b=\operatorname{trdeg}_R S$. Adding and cancelling the finite $h_r$ (by [lem-trf-noetherian-prime-finite-height]) gives $h_q+t\leq h_p+\operatorname{trdeg}_R S$. The one-generator degrees are finite: the generic degree is $0$ or $1$, and the residue degree is bounded by the polynomial equality or quotient inequality and the finite base height. Induction and the two tower identities keep both degrees finite. Hence rearranging this additive inequality is exactly the displayed subtraction inequality, without truncated subtraction.
